records.subagent_summary: My 8 public rollouts scored 1/8 (execution 149.218): six of the seven failures argued that a holder of v plus one fixed reading could just subtract or divide, declared that reading contradictory, collapsed to the other reading, and boxed an arbitrary factor (143 five times), while three burned the 16384-token cap looping on that same contradiction. None ever converted an announcement into a reusable condition on the speaker's value or re-applied it to the partner slot, and none allowed the two private values to be equal; the revision keeps the incumbent's short per-speaker frame and adds exactly those two missing steps.

Seven of eight rollouts scored 1; the single failure reached the modulus step immediately and then took the nth root of the constant by reading it as a familiar base to a smaller exponent, landing on a ratio that was too large by a factor. It ran the incumbent coordinate route flawlessly on that wrong ratio, produced a self-consistent circle, and every self-check it ran confirmed the derived condition rather than the constant, so the error never surfaced. The revision therefore keeps the kept round-7 coordinate route intact and replaces its generic ordering caveat with a named silent-failure warning plus one portable arithmetic check: multiply the candidate ratio by itself n times and require it to land exactly on the modulus of the constant, never a remembered radical.

Round-11 training scored 2/8; the six failures split into two related errors the incumbent does not block. Three argued the shapes are disjoint (overlap 0) by treating the shared point as a center and comparing a point-to-side distance against the small shape's half-width, one of them committing the summed-areas value outright; the other three burned the 16384-token cap oscillating between an unclosed tangency/far-edge-line search and a containment claim, and one had already reached a correct union before abandoning it. The incumbent forbids only overlap = all of S and gives no floor, so this revision adds the strict lower bound (a corner at an interior point covers a positive-angle sector), names the corner-vs-center distance fallacy, fixes axes on the corner's own edges so far edges are provably irrelevant, and makes the first computed orientation a committed anchor that only another computed area may displace.

My 8 public rollouts with the incumbent scored 3/8: two failures terminated normally and two of the three truncations ended the same way, all four collapsing to the family size N because they imposed the progression's common difference on a single function's own consecutive values, concluded the function 'would have to be linear', and inferred one term per function. One truncation had already derived the per-group product and then spent the rest of its budget re-litigating it against that same false obstruction. The revision keeps the proven grouping/root-bound/tightness skeleton but adds the missing fact that the constraint is purely pointwise (finitely many agreements with the target do not force equality) plus an explicit discard rule for the 'P must be linear, so the answer is N' chain.

7/8 public rollouts correct (train_i=0.875); the lone failure fit the parameters, reduced correctly and found the right vertex abscissa, then read that vertex's height with the exponent's sign flipped and took the partner vertex's height by adding the carried gap instead of from f, so both new points were off the graph and the area was wrong. Independently evaluating f at both new vertices would have exposed it immediately, since their difference then contradicts the imposed gap, so the revision replaces the incumbent's bare take-heights-from-f line with that cheap two-point consistency closure while leaving the proven base-normalization and degenerate-root reduction levers intact.

All 8 rollouts scored 0: five modelled the outcome as a uniformly random permutation (1/24) and read part b off it as 1/4, while two claimed the order is deterministic (0/1). The distinctive new failure was that three rollouts assumed the first item reaching the final pile must be the source's top item, so they answered 0 or a bare 1/2; the revision therefore keeps the incumbent's near-minimal length and its 1/2-per-free-step pricing but adds the one missing mechanism, that the middle pile accumulates so arrival rank is set by how many inward moves precede each outward move.

3/8 correct; all three winners simply solved n=2,3,4 numerically and fit the pattern, while all five failures abandoned the numeric ladder for symbolic general-n algebra (parameterized polynomials, elementary symmetric sums, coefficient-of-x formulas) and looped on the resulting contradictions until the token cap. Two failures explicitly trusted a general-n derivation over a small case they had verified, labelling that case exceptional or the system inconsistent, and one fit a law from only two data points and so missed the growth rate entirely. The revision therefore bans symbolic/general-n work outright, demands four back-substituted numeric cases, replaces formula-guessing with consecutive ratios so the growth rate and sign come out mechanically, and makes a verified toy authoritative over any general derivation.

7/8 public rollouts were correct, and the single failure was a new mode, not the old group-count substitution: it ran the incumbent's spine correctly, computed the gcd, factored N as groups times units-per-group, enumerated both admissible counts, and then declared the choice ambiguous and picked the smaller candidate in its final paragraph, reasoning that the smaller one also divided every total evenly. The incumbent asserts the maximum is intended but gives no reason to reject a rival that survives divisibility, and rounds 5-9 showed that adding more anti-substitution apparatus collapses heldout (0.2125 down to 0.0625-0.1375). So I kept the incumbent's spine, ordering and length and spent the budget on a portable maximality-commitment rule: every smaller divisor passes the same check, so passing it is not evidence, and the selection must not be reopened at the end.

All 8 public rollouts under the incumbent were correct (8/8, 3.5k-7.2k tokens, none truncated), so the training question is saturated and remaining gains are transfer. The jointly visible waste is jargon-free: the 7.2k outlier mis-nested the composition (raising the outer coefficient, giving AB^3=BA^9 and B=+-A^4), then integer-guessed four centers, while six of eight rollouts spent their tails hunting 'another fixed point'. Only 2 of 8 ever substituted a known-value input into the identity, and those two closed fastest. Rounds 9 and 10 both spent tokens on composition-exponent audits and both lost heldout, so this revision keeps the proven trigger, centered ansatz, factored both-branch condition, parameter-count closure and symmetric-combination steps, and adds one portable positive move - propagate known values through the identity - which gives progress on unseen functional-equation problems where no centered ansatz fits.

Only 1/8 correct and 7 of 8 failures ended at the 16384-token cap; the most telling one had already reached a correct closed form inside its reasoning block, then spent the whole remaining budget restating a formal write-up from scratch and was truncated before re-boxing it. The others never committed, looping dozens of times over the same size with mutually inconsistent counts and re-arguing in prose instead of redoing one cheap simulation, and several burned tokens worrying about "any word". The revision keeps the incumbent's state-rewriting and anti-involution mechanisms but adds that one distinct-label word suffices, a per-label divisibility check on the count, and a budget rule to box the answer as soon as a formula fits rather than re-deriving it.
